raw_case_text:
A 20-year-old male with immune-mediated aplastic anemia refractory to prior immune suppression therapy received an unrelated donor peripheral stem cell transplant. Toxoplasma serologies were not obtained during his pre-transplant evaluation as per institutional practice. His initial transplant course was uncomplicated, and he was discharged home on post-transplant day +21. On day +52, he was readmitted for fever and diarrhea. Due to fever and hypoxemia, a CT scan of the chest was obtained on day +55 and showed bilateral centrilobular nodules with right-sided predominance, as shown in Figure 1C. His infectious workup included multiple BALs, blood, and urine cultures and evaluation for Pneumocystis jirovecii and viral etiologies, which were all negative. He was maintained on broad-spectrum antibiotics and antifungal medications given the persistent fever despite negative cultures. Due to progressive hypoxemic respiratory failure, he was transferred to the PICU on day +61, where he required intubation and mechanical ventilation. Given the refractory hypoxemic respiratory failure, he was cannulated to venous-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) within 24 h of PICU transfer. His ECMO course was complicated by shock, hyperferritinemia, and acute kidney injury requiring renal replacement therapy.
Multimodal therapy for his immune dysregulation included pulse dose methylprednisolone (2 g/day) followed by a prolonged methylprednisolone course, plasma exchange, tocilizumab for IL-6 blockade, and etanercept for tumor necrosis factor alpha blockade, which was later transitioned to infliximab. A timeline of the immunomodulatory therapies is shown in Figure 2B. With improvement in his hyperinflammatory state, he was decannulated from ECMO on day +73.
On day +90, he had recurrence of fever without other changes in exam in the setting of a methylprednisolone taper; after a multidisciplinary discussion, tocilizumab, infliximab, and pulse dose methylprednisolone were administered for the management of immune dysregulation. The results of his clinical cytokine panel from day +64 to +92 are shown in Table 1. Despite these interventions, he had worsening hyperferritinemia by day +94 (peak level, 202,000 ng/mL), so anakinra was administered and plasma exchange was repeated. Despite immunomodulation, he continued to have refractory MODS with severe hypoxemic respiratory failure and catecholamine-refractory shock. At the request of his family, resuscitative efforts were discontinued on day +95. On the day of his death, T. gondii tachyzoites were noted on his peripheral blood smear (shown in Figure 1D), which were subsequently confirmed to be T. gondii by PCR and immunostaining. Postmortem analyses of the BAL specimens from day +60 and +65 were also positive for T. gondii by PCR. Postmortem T. gondii serologic testing was performed on a pre-transplant blood specimen and was positive for IgG.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 20-year-old male with refractory immune-mediated aplastic anemia presented on day +52 after unrelated-donor peripheral blood stem cell transplantation with fever, diarrhea, and progressive hypoxemic respiratory failure.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Following an uncomplicated initial course after an unrelated-donor peripheral blood stem cell transplant for refractory aplastic anemia (discharged on day +21 without pre-transplant Toxoplasma serologic screening), the patient was readmitted on day +52 with fever and diarrhea, rapidly developing hypoxemia by day +55 and refractory hypoxemic respiratory failure requiring PICU intubation and veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) cannulation on day +61.
subjective.past_medical_history: Refractory immune-mediated aplastic anemia status post unrelated-donor peripheral blood stem cell transplantation.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, diarrhea, and severe progressive dyspnea/hypoxemia.

objective.physical_examination: Febrile and hypoxemic on day +55, progressing to catecholamine-refractory shock and severe hypoxemic respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation and VV-ECMO on day +61 (decannulated day +73, with recurrent febrile shock and MODS on days +90 to +95).
objective.routine_investigations: Routine microbiological and hyperinflammatory workup: Multiple blood, urine, and BAL cultures and evaluations for Pneumocystis jirovecii and viruses were negative; severe hyperferritinemia peaking at 202,000 ng/mL on day +94 with marked hypercytokinemia (days +64 to +92) and acute kidney injury requiring renal replacement therapy. Day +95 peripheral blood smear (on day of death): Directly visualized circulating extracellular/intracellular Toxoplasma gondii tachyzoites.
objective.advanced_workup: Day +55 chest CT: Bilateral centrilobular pulmonary nodules with right-sided predominance. Post-mortem molecular and serological confirmation: Peripheral blood smear tachyzoites were confirmed as Toxoplasma gondii by PCR and immunostaining; retrospective PCR analysis of stored BAL specimens from days +60 and +65 tested positive for T. gondii; retrospective testing of stored pre-transplant serum was positive for T. gondii IgG.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Fatal reactivated disseminated toxoplasmosis and Toxoplasma pneumonia masquerading as idiopathic post-transplant hyperinflammatory immune dysregulation / secondary HLH (peak ferritin 202,000 ng/mL) requiring VV-ECMO after unrelated-donor stem cell transplantation for aplastic anemia, definitively diagnosed on day +95 by T. gondii tachyzoites on peripheral blood smear (confirmed by PCR/immunostaining) and retrospective positive T. gondii PCR on day +60/+65 BAL fluid (with Pneumocystis jirovecii excluded). Plan and clinical course: Managed on VV-ECMO (days +61 to +73) and CRRT with broad-spectrum antibacterials/antifungals and intensive anti-cytokine immunomodulation (pulse methylprednisolone 2 g/day, plasma exchange, tocilizumab, etanercept, infliximab, and anakinra), which transiently allowed ECMO decannulation on day +73 before a fatal relapse of refractory shock and MODS on days +90 to +95.
